estimated_row_count_rationale: IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File contains 1,923,040+ tax-exempt organizations as of November 2025, but filtering for $50K+ annual revenue (medium-to-large nonprofits most likely to purchase B2B software/services, excluding tiny all-volunteer orgs under $50K) yields approximately 360,000 active public charities, social welfare orgs, and other tax-exempt entities. Form 990 Part VII Section A requires disclosure of all officers, directors, trustees, key employees, and five highest compensated employees — typical nonprofit organizational structure includes: 1 Executive Director/CEO, 1 Development Director/CDO (at orgs $500K+ revenue), 1 CFO/Treasurer (at orgs $1M+ revenue), 1-2 Program Directors/VPs (at larger orgs), 1 Board Chair, 1 Secretary, 5-15 additional Trustees/Directors depending on org size and complexity. Averaging 8-12 board members + 2-4 executives per organization (larger orgs like hospitals and universities have 15-25 board members + 8-12 C-suite executives, smaller $100K-$500K orgs have 5-7 board members + 1-2 staff), conservative estimate yields 1.5 decision-makers per organization (some small orgs have only 1-2 officers listed, large orgs have 20-30 total Part VII individuals). 360,000 orgs × 1.5 average contacts = 540,000 rows. Adding state charity registry supplemental contacts (some states require listing of all board members even if not on 990, plus alternate contact emails) and cross-referencing ProPublica People Search to capture individuals serving on multiple nonprofit boards pushes total to 550,000-600,000 records. One row per individual per organization — a person serving on 3 nonprofit boards appears 3 times (once per org) since buyer use case is 'reach all decision-makers at healthcare nonprofits' not 'deduplicate individuals.' Target output focuses on decision-maker titles only (exclude administrative staff, program coordinators, volunteers listed in Part VII but lacking budget authority for software/service purchases).
source_url_rationale: IRS Form 990 Series Downloads (irs.gov/charities-non-profits/form-990-series-downloads) provide complete bulk XML files for all electronically filed 990s from 2010-present, organized by year and month — Part VII Section A contains structured data on all officers, directors, trustees, key employees with name, title, hours per week, and compensation (100% public disclosure mandated by IRC Section 6104, zero authentication required, direct bulk download available). IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File (irs.gov/charities-non-profits/exempt-organizations-business-master-file-extract-eo-bmf) is authoritative registry of all 1.9M+ tax-exempt organizations with EIN, legal name, mailing address, state, ruling date, asset amount, income amount, NTEE classification code, foundation code (public charity vs. private foundation), tax period — updated monthly as CSV download, public domain federal data. ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (projects.propublica.org/nonprofits) provides searchable interface to millions of 990 returns with 'People Search' feature enabling lookup of individuals across all filings to identify board members serving on multiple nonprofits — database updated April 2026, includes executive compensation, revenue, expenses, full-text search, and organization profiles with multi-year trend data (100% public, mirrors IRS bulk data with enhanced search UI). State charity registration databases (California AG Registry of Charitable Trusts at oag.ca.gov/charities/registry, New York Charities Bureau at charitiesnys.com, Massachusetts AGO, Texas Secretary of State, Florida Division of Consumer Services) contain additional contact information beyond IRS filings such as primary contact email, phone, responsible officer name, registered agent, website URL — required for nonprofits soliciting donations in each state, public records under state sunshine laws with free online lookup and bulk download options in some states. All sources are 100% public with zero legal restrictions: federal law mandates 990 disclosure, IRS provides free bulk downloads, state charity registrations are public records under open records statutes — no scraping behind authentication, no purchased private datasets, no FOIA requests needed.

engineering_notes: Download IRS Form 990 XML bulk files from irs.gov/charities-non-profits/form-990-series-downloads (organized by year 2010-2025, current year by month) — parse Part VII Section A 'Officers, Directors, Trustees, Key Employees, and Highest Compensated Employees' using XPath queries to extract PersonNm, TitleTxt, AverageHoursPerWeekRt, ReportableCompFromOrgAmt, ReportableCompFromRltdOrgAmt, OtherCompensationAmt per individual. Download IRS EO BMF CSV from irs.gov/charities-non-profits/exempt-organizations-business-master-file-extract-eo-bmf — join on EIN to append organization metadata (legal name, DBA, mailing address, state, ZIP, asset amount, income amount, NTEE classification, foundation code, ruling date, tax period). Filter for organizations with INCOME_AMT >= $50,000 to exclude tiny all-volunteer nonprofits unlikely to purchase B2B software/services. Cross-reference ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer API (if available) or scrape organization profile pages for supplemental contact data and multi-year officer history to infer years-in-role. Scrape or bulk-download state charity registration databases: California oag.ca.gov/charities/registry (Registry Search by name, downloadable reports), New York charitiesnys.com (searchable by name/EIN), Massachusetts, Texas, Florida — extract primary contact email, phone, responsible officer, registered agent, website URL to supplement IRS base records. Normalize job titles to standard taxonomy (map 'President' → 'Board Chair', 'Chief Executive Officer' → 'Executive Director', 'VP of Development' → 'Development Director', 'Chief Financial Officer' → 'CFO', etc.) using keyword pattern matching. Deduplicate individuals serving same role at same org across multiple 990 filing years (keep most recent year only). Do NOT deduplicate individuals across different organizations (person serving on 3 boards appears 3 times per buyer use case). Geocode mailing addresses via Census geocoder API or Nominatim for lat/lon coordinates. Classify NTEE codes into human-readable subsector categories (A=Arts, B=Education, C=Environment, E=Health, P=Human Services, X=Religion, etc.). Enrich missing individual emails via LinkedIn profile scraping (search 'Development Director at [Org Name]'), ZoomInfo/Apollo business directory lookups for org domain, and pattern-based guessing (firstname.lastname@orgdomain.com validated via email verification API). Flag organizations requiring federal Single Audit (income >= $750K AND received federal grants based on 990 Schedule I). Estimated engineering time: 60-80 hours (moderate-to-high complexity due to XML parsing across thousands of 990 files, state registry scraping with varying schemas, title normalization logic, email enrichment workflows, but all core data sources are structured public databases with bulk download access — no unstructured web scraping or authentication bypass required).
compliance_notes: Zero PII — all data is organizational officer/director information publicly disclosed in IRS Form 990 tax returns (federal law IRC Section 6104 mandates public disclosure of all 990s, available via IRS bulk downloads and third-party mirrors like ProPublica) and state charity registration filings (public records under state sunshine laws for consumer protection — donors verify charity legitimacy and officer credentials before giving). Names and titles are disclosed BY THE NONPROFITS THEMSELVES in regulatory filings for transparency and accountability purposes — no expectation of privacy for nonprofit executives and board members whose roles inherently involve public trust and fiduciary duties. Contact information (phone, email) sourced from state charity registries where nonprofits voluntarily provide business contact details for donation solicitation and compliance correspondence, or enriched from publicly accessible business directories (LinkedIn profiles self-published by executives, organization websites listing staff/board bios with contact forms). No personal home addresses, personal phone numbers, personal emails, or sensitive financial data (individual bank accounts, SSNs, personal tax info) — only organizational mailing addresses (nonprofit office locations publicly listed) and business contact information. No GDPR applicability (U.S. nonprofits and business contacts, not EU individuals). Automatic PASS expected from compliance-officer — dataset consists entirely of publicly mandated regulatory disclosures with zero sensitive data, aligning perfectly with 'public data only' hard rule and 'no PII' compliance gate.
